title: Persist the Foundation attempt journal authority
description: Prerequisite for task-af9454f4438242e5854208284e0086e2. Current measurement at HEAD a42ae2f: `journal.append` exists in the frozen RuntimeCommandKind union and @moe/context exports `createDeadEndJournal`, but daemon has no production journal writer/reader and no attempt journalDigest. Deliverable: an authenticated, attempt/session/lease-bound journal application service and durable reader using the public @moe/context canonical journal, so safe release can bind the exact current digest rather than a caller/fixed value. Consumer: task-af9454f4438242e5854208284e0086e2.
definitionOfDone: A production `journal.append` path authenticates first, checks the exact capability/payload allow-list, derives project/session/attempt/node/lease from durable authority, and persists only entries admitted by public `createDeadEndJournal`; no new wire kind is added.
The durable journal is bounded, canonical and append-only; its digest covers the exact ordered entries, and a strict current reader returns the attempt-bound digest/record from canonical bytes.

Caller-selected project, lease, graph, digest, truth class or replacement journal is structurally refused; stale session/lease, absent attempt, conflicting append, malformed entry, limit excess and unreadable/ambiguous storage each assert a stable exact code and refusing layer.
Same command bytes replay without another entry; conflicting bytes refuse before mutation, and raw event/decision counts plus canonical bytes prove the original survives.

Real SqliteEventStore + Authenticator tests include one accepted append/control, empty-current-journal semantics, nonzero hostile cases, zero residue, and a mutation where the digest ignores an entry that reddens a named assertion.
Completion names task-af9454f4438242e5854208284e0086e2 as the reader consumer; daemon typecheck/test run separately and print nonzero test counts.
taskRails: Use the existing frozen `journal.append` kind and public @moe/context root; do not add a wire kind, copy journal canonicalization, or accept a caller digest.
Authentication precedes payload authority. Preserve authenticator/registry/context refusal code and layer rather than restamping.
The daemon command registry is already near the split limit; extract a focused registry fragment before 400 rather than growing a monolith.
TDD exact codes/layers, real SqliteEventStore, target <=250 lines per production source, explicit owned-path commits.

implementationPlan.description:
LAND THE DEPENDENCY EDGE, then verify-or-block. `@moe/context` is NOT a dependency of `@moe/daemon` at HEAD — measured, see planningNotes. This step is first because nothing else compiles without it.
(a) Add `"@moe/context": "workspace:*"` to apps/daemon/package.json dependencies (alphabetical: after @moe/contracts... place it so the block stays sorted as the file already is).
(b) Run `pnpm install` at the repo root and confirm the pnpm-lock.yaml diff is limited to the apps/daemon importer block — `git diff --stat pnpm-lock.yaml`. A wide lock churn means the install did something else; stop and report it rather than committing it.
(c) Compiled bare-specifier probe: write apps/daemon/src/journal/_edge-probe.ts containing `import { createDeadEndJournal, DEAD_END_KINDS } from "@moe/context"; export const probe = [createDeadEndJournal, DEAD_END_KINDS];`, run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, expect EXIT=0, DELETE the probe in the same command. A root-barrel grep does NOT satisfy this leg — and note that `packages/context/src/index.ts` is five `export *` lines, so grepping it for a symbol name returns a FALSE NEGATIVE.
(d) Re-measure the gap in both directions before writing code: `grep -rln journal --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src` must return only test/fixture files (no production writer or reader); `grep -rn journalDigest --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src | grep -v test` must return zero; `grep -n 'journal.append' packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` must still return the frozen union member. If a production journal path now exists, block instead of duplicating it.
Record every command and its result — they are the completion evidence for the dependency-edge rail.

Land apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-contracts.ts plus its one-line bridge `export * from "./journal-contracts.ts";` (a .ts module without its .js bridge is invisible to consumers while tsc and vitest both stay green). This file carries the validation bulk so the service module stays under the per-file cap.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_COMMAND_KIND` annotated as `RuntimeCommandKind` from @moe/contracts so a typo fails to compile; do NOT add a wire kind.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_SCHEMA_VERSION = "moe-journal-append/1"`, `JOURNAL_RECORD_VERSION = "moe-attempt-journal/1"`, `JOURNAL_APPEND_EVENT_TYPE = "AttemptJournalAppended"`.
- `JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS = ["attemptAggregateId", "effectId", "entries"]` — EXACTLY these three. projectId, sessionId, leaseRef, graphRef, journalDigest, truthClass and a replacement `journal` are deliberately absent, which is what makes them structurally refused by the seam's `checkPayload` allow-list under ITS `PAYLOAD_SHAPE` code rather than by anything downstream.
- `DAEMON_JOURNAL_APPEND` layer constant, and a frozen closed code list: JOURNAL_REQUEST_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_ENTRY_LIST_EMPTY, JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH, JOURNAL_NODE_UNREADABLE, JOURNAL_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE, JOURNAL_RECORD_ABSENT, JOURNAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE, JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED, JOURNAL_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS, JOURNAL_PROJECT_MISMATCH, JOURNAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
- `deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(activationDigest)`: length-framed sha256, same shape as `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId`. Keyed on the ACTIVATION DIGEST because that value is server-derived and coherence-checked by the binding reader, so no caller can name a journal stream into existence.
- THE STRICT ENTRY DECODER, and it is load-bearing: `createDeadEndJournal` performs NO shape validation. Its `clonePredicate` switches on `predicate.kind` and returns `undefined` for an unknown kind, and `canonicalSha256` THROWS on `undefined` (`Unsupported canonical value type`). An unvalidated entry therefore CRASHES the command instead of refusing it, and a crash is not a refusal. Decode each entry over own data properties: exact 11 keys (id, kind, failureCode, primaryScope, recipeDigest, baseDigest, environmentDigest, retryPredicate, text, actorId, occurredAt); `kind` must be a member of `DEAD_END_KINDS` IMPORTED from @moe/context (never retyped locally); `retryPredicate` exact-keyed per its `kind` against @moe/context's `FactPredicate`; the three digest fields lowercase hex64; `occurredAt` an ISO instant ending in Z; `text` a bounded string. Anything else -> JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED. An empty `entries` array -> JOURNAL_ENTRY_LIST_EMPTY.

Land the WRITER in apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-append.ts plus its `export * from "./journal-append.ts";` bridge: `runJournalAppendCommand(store, bytes)`, matching the shape of the other registry-dispatched services (server-assembled request bytes in, `{ok, decision, disposition}` or a refusal out).
Order is the contract, and each stage keeps the refusing layer's OWN code:
1. Decode the request bytes: bounded JSON, exact envelope keys, `kind` and `schemaVersion` match -> JOURNAL_REQUEST_MALFORMED otherwise. projectId, principalId and decidedAt are SERVER facts already stamped by the registry's `requestOf`; never read them from the payload.
2. Payload exact keys per JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS.
3. `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, payload.effectId, principalId, Date.parse(decidedAt))` from ../activation/activation-ledger-reader.js. Not BOUND -> return ITS code (FOUNDATION_BINDING_LEASE_INACTIVE / _LEASE_EXPIRED / _TERMINAL / _NOT_FOUND / _QUERY_MISMATCH / _PROJECT_MISMATCH ...) and ITS layer VERBATIM. Do not restamp: a stale lease must stay distinguishable from an absent attempt. This one call is what makes the append attempt/session/lease-bound — it requires intent ACTIVE, attempt RUNNING, lease ACTIVE, lease not past its wall deadline, and a coherent activation, all from committed evidence.
4. Derive the durable attempt facts: `store.readEvents(payload.attemptAggregateId)` then `readFoundationActivationHistory(aggregateId, events, projectId)`. Cross-check `record.activationDigest === binding.activationDigest`, `record.effectIntent.intentId === binding.effectId`, `record.lease.ownerSessionRef === binding.sessionId`; any mismatch -> JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH. attemptRef = `record.attempt.attemptId`, leaseRef = `record.lease.leaseId` — the caller's aggregate id only LOCATES; the activation-digest equality is what forbids pointing at someone else's attempt.
5. nodeKey from durable evidence: read `deriveDispatchAggregateId(payload.attemptAggregateId)` (from ../work/foundation-attempt-codec.js), take the exactly-one `FoundationDispatchReserved` event, decode + re-encode + sameBytes, read `nodeKey`. Zero, two, or drifted bytes -> JOURNAL_NODE_UNREADABLE. The RESERVED event is written at dispatch, so it exists for a live attempt.
6. Decode the caller entries with the step-3 strict decoder.
7. Read the CURRENT durable journal (step 5's reader). ABSENT means an empty entry list and is NOT an error here; every other refusal propagates unchanged.
8. `createDeadEndJournal([...current.entries, ...admittedEntries])`. A REFUSED result keeps its own `JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED` code and `DEAD_END_JOURNAL` layer verbatim — do not restamp, do not truncate, do not retry with fewer entries.
9. Compose the body from DURABLE facts only: recordVersion, projectId, sessionId, effectId, attemptRef, leaseRef, nodeKey, activationDigest, entries (the ADMITTED, canonically ordered ones), journalDigest (the admitted journal's own digest), truthClass "DAEMON_VERIFIED". Canonical bytes via `encodeFoundationPayload`; drift -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED.
10. Commit ONE event on `deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(binding.activationDigest)` at `expectedVersion` = current event count, key `{commandId, principalId, projectId}`. Append-only: never rewrite a prior event. Throw or non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED -> JOURNAL_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE.
11. Answer from the reader — never from the value just written.

Land the STRICT CURRENT READER `readCurrentAttemptJournal(store, activationDigest, expectedProjectId)` in the same module. If journal-append.ts would cross 250 physical lines, split the reader into apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-reader.ts plus its .js bridge — that split is AUTHORIZED by this plan; record the measured line count as the forcing evidence in the completion notes, since the per-FILE cap is hard and the per-task file count is not a reason to breach it.
Algorithm, fail-closed at every branch:
- `store.readEvents(deriveAttemptJournalAggregateId(activationDigest))` in try/catch -> JOURNAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE on throw; zero events -> JOURNAL_RECORD_ABSENT (distinct from UNREADABLE: no rows and an unreadable store demand opposite repairs).
- Every event must be `AttemptJournalAppended` with `aggregateSequence === index + 1`; a foreign type or a sequence hole -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED; two events claiming the same sequence -> JOURNAL_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS.
- The CURRENT journal is the LAST event. Decode -> re-encode -> `sameBytes(again.bytes, event.payload)`; drift -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED. Canonical bytes need both the digest and the re-encode.
- Body exact-keyed; recordVersion mismatch -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED; body projectId !== expectedProjectId -> JOURNAL_PROJECT_MISMATCH.
- RE-DERIVE the digest through the production surface: run `createDeadEndJournal(body.entries)` and compare `journal.digest` with the stored `journalDigest`; unequal -> JOURNAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH; REFUSED -> JOURNAL_RECORD_MALFORMED. This is what makes a stored digest that has quietly stopped covering its entries unusable rather than merely wrong, and it is where the DoD's digest mutation drill lands.
- Answer frozen: `{ ok: true, authority: "DURABLE_JOURNAL", journalDigest, entries, attemptRef, leaseRef, nodeKey, sessionId, effectId, activationDigest }`. Every refused branch returns authority "NONE" and no digest — an unverifiable journal never becomes a handoff input.
Tests: ABSENT before any append; UNREADABLE on a throwing store; MALFORMED on a planted drifted payload; AMBIGUOUS on a duplicated sequence; PROJECT_MISMATCH on a foreign expected project; DIGEST_MISMATCH on a planted body whose entries and digest disagree — each pinning the exact code AND the exact layer.

Wire the command into the seam, and update the closed roster it breaks.
In apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts, keep the delta to roughly ten lines by importing the registration data from the journal fragment rather than inlining new literals — the file is 346 lines and the task rail requires extracting a focused fragment rather than growing the monolith. Add: JOURNAL_APPEND_COMMAND_KIND to `WiredCommandKind`; a PAYLOAD_KEYS entry sourced from JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS; a `journal` branch in `entryOf` supplying JOURNAL_APPEND_SCHEMA_VERSION, `requiredCapability` = `work.write`, and `decisionOf(runJournalAppendCommand(store, bytes))`; and a `journal` case in `agentCapabilitiesFor` returning `[work.write]`. Do NOT add it to OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS: an agent holding work authority is exactly who appends a dead-end journal. If the file crosses 380 lines, move the journal branch out into the fragment as a handler factory instead of inlining it.
THE ROSTER WILL GO RED AND THAT IS EXPECTED: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts asserts "exactly the twenty-three characterized kinds", with `ROWS` at length 23 and `registry.size` 23 at two separate places (lines ~167-171 and ~419). Add the `journal.append` ROW with its capability and payload keys and bump BOTH counts to 24. Do not weaken the roster into a `>=` check — its whole value is that a new kind cannot be registered unnoticed.
After wiring, the step-2 accepted-append control must go green through the real seam, which is also the proof that authentication and the capability check run BEFORE any payload authority: the seam's order is authenticate -> AUTHORIZE/CAPABILITY_DENIED -> `checkPayload` -> dispatch.

THE REFUSAL MATRIX — DoD item 3. Every case asserts the exact code, the exact refusing LAYER, and zero durable residue (the journal aggregate's event count is unchanged).
Structural refusals, which must be answered by the SEAM's allow-list and not by the service: a payload carrying `projectId`, `leaseRef`, `graphRef`, `journalDigest`, `truthClass`, or a whole replacement `journal` object is refused at PAYLOAD_SHAPE. Assert the seam's own code and that `runJournalAppendCommand` was never reached — a refusal answered one layer earlier than the test believes is the classic vacuous assertion, so pin WHICH layer answered.
Domain refusals: a session whose lease has expired (advance the clock past `serverWallDeadline`); a session that is not the lease owner; an attempt whose intent is no longer ACTIVE or whose attempt is not RUNNING; an absent attempt aggregate; an `attemptAggregateId` naming a DIFFERENT live attempt than `effectId` (JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH — this is the one that proves the caller's aggregate id only locates and never authorises); a malformed entry (bad `kind`, unknown `retryPredicate.kind`, non-hex digest, extra key); an empty entries array; entries exceeding MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRY_COUNT and, separately, MAX_JOURNAL_TEXT_CHARACTERS — both keeping @moe/context's `JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED` / `DEAD_END_JOURNAL` code and layer verbatim, with `limit` naming which bound was hit.
The unknown-predicate case is the important one: assert it is a REFUSAL with JOURNAL_ENTRY_MALFORMED, not a thrown `TypeError` from `canonicalSha256`. A test that only asserts "it did not succeed" would pass on a crash.

Idempotence, conflict, and the hostile sweep — DoD item 4.
- REPLAY: issue the same command bytes twice. Assert the second is REPLAYED, the journal aggregate's raw event count is unchanged, the entry list is unchanged, and `journalDigest` is byte-identical. Read the counts from the store, not from the command result.
- CONFLICTING BYTES: reuse the same commandId with different entries. Assert it refuses BEFORE mutating — raw event count unchanged, and the reader still returns the ORIGINAL entries and digest. The store's idempotency conflict keeps its own code and DURABLE_STORE layer rather than being flattened into a journal code.
- APPEND ORDERING: a second, genuinely new append adds one event, and the reader returns the union in `createDeadEndJournal`'s canonical order (occurredAt, then id, then entry digest) — assert against the production ordering by feeding the same entries to `createDeadEndJournal` directly, not against a hand-sorted literal.
- GENERATED HOSTILE SWEEP over the entry and payload surface: per field emit mutations (missing key, extra key, wrong type, -0, NaN, non-NFC text, `__proto__` key, accessor-bearing entry, revoked-proxy entry, uppercase digest, `occurredAt` without Z, entry count at the limit and one over). Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing — and assert every case refuses with a code from the frozen list under a named layer, never a throw.
- Close every store in a `finally` on every exit path; a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker with an error that looks unrelated.

MUTATION DRILLS — a green suite cannot show that these assertions are still attached to their subject. Run each, record the exact test name that reddened, restore, and confirm the restored bytes hash-match the original (git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree).
1. DoD item 5's required drill: make the persisted digest ignore an entry — compose the body with `createDeadEndJournal(entries.slice(0, -1)).journal.digest` while storing all entries. A NAMED test must redden; this is exactly what the reader's re-derivation exists to catch.
2. Delete the strict entry decode and pass caller entries straight to `createDeadEndJournal`. The unknown-predicate test must redden — and confirm it reddens as a REFUSAL assertion, not merely because the process threw.
3. Replace the activation cross-check in step 4 with `true`. The JOURNAL_BINDING_MISMATCH test must redden.
4. Change the binding call to ignore the lease deadline (pass a fixed early `nowMilliseconds`). The lease-expired test must redden; if it does not, the test is asserting a refusal some earlier layer is answering.
5. Widen JOURNAL_APPEND_PAYLOAD_KEYS to include `journalDigest`. A structural-refusal test must redden — this proves the caller-digest fence is the allow-list and not an accident.
If a drill survives, do not rationalise it: either the assertion has detached from its subject or the mutation is equivalent. Say which, with evidence, in the completion notes.

REGRESSION AND GATE. Registering a new command kind touches the seam roster and every test that enumerates registered kinds, and adding a workspace dependency touches install state — so run the whole daemon package, not just the new file.
Run exactly:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; TC=$?; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; TT=$?; echo "TYPECHECK=$TC TEST=$TT"`
Both exit codes captured separately — do not pipe (a piped run reports the pipe tail's code) and do not `&&`-chain (a red typecheck then hides the test count line). READ THE OUTPUT: the test leg must print a `Test Files ... passed` count line with a NONZERO count. `pnpm --filter` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 when the package does not resolve, so exit 0 with no count line is UNVERIFIED, not passing. @moe/daemon resolves to apps/daemon.
Also run `pnpm --filter @moe/context test` once as a positive control that the new dependency did not disturb the producer package.
Then attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline: repo-wide failures at the merge-base, again at HEAD, and confirm the delta intersected with this task's owned paths is EMPTY. Report any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and paths; never hide it and never fabricate green. A red your own diff caused in a foreign file is NOT excused — that is exactly what the delta detects.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker:
- Can a caller get a project, lease, graph ref, digest, truth class or a whole replacement journal into durable bytes on ANY path? Trace every persisted field back to the binding reader, the activation record, the dispatch RESERVED event, or `createDeadEndJournal`'s admitted output.
- Two appends racing on the same attempt: does `expectedVersion` = current count make the loser conflict rather than both landing? Does a replay of the winner still return the same digest?
- Does any refusal path write bytes before refusing? Every refusal test must also assert an unchanged raw event count.
- Is any refusal restamped? A stale lease must still read as the binding reader's own code and layer, and a limit excess as `JOURNAL_LIMIT_REACHED` / `DEAD_END_JOURNAL`.
- Confirm every production file is under 250 physical lines (split before 400), that the step-1 `_edge-probe.ts` is gone, and that no scratch or generated file remains.
COMPLETION MUST RECORD, per the consumer-edge rail: task-af9454f4438242e5854208284e0086e2 is the named reader consumer, and its exact edge is `readCurrentAttemptJournal(store, activationDigest, projectId)` from apps/daemon/src/journal/journal-append.js, whose `journalDigest` is the lowercase hex64 `canonicalSha256` that satisfies BOTH @moe/context's `createReleaseHandoff` 64-hex `journalDigest` reference check (packages/context/src/release-handoff.ts) and @moe/scheduler's `ReleaseHandoff.journalDigest` key (packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:47), replacing the caller/fixed value that path has no other source for. Also record the four fail-closed codes and their layer.
Stage and commit ONLY the owned paths by explicit pathspec — including apps/daemon/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml, which this task genuinely owns. Never `git add -A`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) ADD A NEW WIRE KIND for the journal. REJECTED by task rail 1 and unnecessary: `journal.append` is already a member of the frozen `RuntimeCommandKind` union at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:96 and is already generated into the control-room client (packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:218). Annotating the constant as `RuntimeCommandKind` makes a typo a compile error.
2) STORE ONLY THE DELTA ENTRIES per append and fold them on read. REJECTED: the reader would have to reconstruct ordering itself, and the DoD asks for a current reader that answers the attempt-bound digest FROM CANONICAL BYTES. Chosen instead: each append persists the whole admitted journal (canonically ordered entries + its digest) as the new head event, and the READER re-derives the digest through `createDeadEndJournal` and refuses on mismatch. That keeps the durable bytes authoritative while making a digest that has quietly stopped covering its entries unusable rather than merely wrong — and it is where the DoD's required digest mutation drill lands.
3) KEY THE JOURNAL AGGREGATE ON A CALLER-SUPPLIED ATTEMPT AGGREGATE ID. REJECTED: a caller could then name a journal stream into existence. Chosen: derive it from `binding.activationDigest`, which `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding` produces from committed evidence and cross-checks for coherence. The caller's `attemptAggregateId` only LOCATES the activation record; the activation-digest equality check is what forbids pointing at another attempt.
4) LET `createDeadEndJournal` VALIDATE THE ENTRIES. REJECTED, and this is the sharpest hazard in the task: it performs NO shape validation. `clonePredicate` switches on `predicate.kind` and returns `undefined` for an unknown kind, and `canonicalSha256` THROWS `Unsupported canonical value type: undefined`. An unvalidated entry crashes the command instead of refusing it, and a crash is not a refusal. The daemon must decode entries strictly first, importing DEAD_END_KINDS and FactPredicate from @moe/context rather than retyping them.
5) GROW daemon-command-registry.ts WITH INLINE LITERALS. REJECTED by task rail 3 — the file is 346 of 400 lines. The journal's registration data (kind, schema version, payload keys, capability) lives in the journal fragment; the registry imports and composes, keeping its delta around ten lines.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 15918c72 (the description's a42ae2f is stale). All three of the description's claims re-measured; two hold, one is WRONG in a way that changes the plan.

DEPENDENCY EDGE IS ABSENT — THE ONE CORRECTION. `apps/daemon/package.json` dependencies are exactly: @moe/contracts, @moe/coordination, @moe/core, @moe/mcp, @moe/review, @moe/runner, @moe/scheduler, @moe/store. **@moe/context is NOT among them.** There is no escape hatch (no tsconfig paths, no project references; a deep relative import fails TS6059), so step 1 lands the manifest edit plus the workspace install and BOTH apps/daemon/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml are owned paths.

CLAIM CONFIRMED: `journal.append` is in the frozen union at packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:96.

CLAIM CONFIRMED, but note the grep trap: `createDeadEndJournal` IS exported from the @moe/context root — packages/context/src/index.ts is five `export *` lines, so grepping that file for the symbol returns a FALSE NEGATIVE. It is defined at packages/context/src/dead-end-journal.ts:108.

GAP CONFIRMED PRESENT: `grep -rln journal --include=*.ts apps/daemon/src` returns only recovery-test-fixtures.ts and attempt-release-disposition.test.ts — no production writer or reader. `grep -rn journalDigest apps/daemon/src` returns one fixture line with `journalDigest: null`.

WHO NEEDS THE DIGEST (the consumer link, measured): `journalDigest` is a REQUIRED field in two production surfaces. @moe/context's `createReleaseHandoff` (packages/context/src/release-handoff.ts:6,17) refuses unless it is a 64-hex content reference, code INVALID_CONTENT_REFERENCE / layer RELEASE_HANDOFF. @moe/scheduler's `ReleaseHandoff` (packages/scheduler/src/authority/lease-drain.ts:47,81,164) lists it among the nine handoff keys the release parser checks. `ExpansionReleaseEvidence` does NOT carry it — the consumer link is the HANDOFF, not the evidence record. `canonicalSha256` returns lowercase hex64, so the admitted journal's own digest satisfies both checks directly.

THE BINDING READER IS THE WHOLE FENCE: `readCurrentEffectSessionBinding(store, projectId, effectId, sessionId, nowMilliseconds)` (apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.ts:316) already requires project match, effect found, intent ACTIVE, attempt RUNNING, lease parsed and equal to the intent's lease binding, lease ACTIVE, lease not past `serverWallDeadline` (seconds, and the deadline second itself is still live), a coherent activation commit, and effectId/sessionId equality — all from committed evidence, with the caller's values used for equality and nothing else. It returns `{activationDigest, effectId, sessionId, status:"BOUND"}`; attemptRef and leaseRef come from `readFoundationActivationHistory` over the attempt aggregate, cross-checked on activationDigest.

NODEKEY IS DURABLY AVAILABLE MID-ATTEMPT: apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts:210-216 commits the `FoundationDispatchReserved` event carrying `{attemptId, grantId, nodeKey}` at dispatch time, on `deriveDispatchAggregateId(attemptAggregateId)`. The RECORDED event is written only at settlement, so read RESERVED, not RECORDED.

THE SEAM ORDER SATISFIES 'AUTHENTICATION PRECEDES PAYLOAD AUTHORITY' ALREADY: apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts authenticates, then refuses AUTHORIZE/CAPABILITY_DENIED, then runs `checkPayload(payload, entry.payloadKeys)` -> PAYLOAD_SHAPE, then dispatches. So an unknown payload key is refused structurally by the seam under its own code — which is exactly how caller-selected project/lease/graph/digest/truthClass/replacement-journal are fenced, provided the allow-list stays the three keys this plan names.

CLOSED ROSTER THAT WILL BREAK: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts asserts "exactly the twenty-three characterized kinds", `ROWS` length 23 and `registry.size` 23 at TWO places (~167-171 and ~419). Registering a 24th kind reddens it by design; add the row and bump both counts rather than weakening the assertion.

TEMPLATE MODULE: apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-release-disposition.ts (249 lines) — own layer constant, frozen closed code list, length-framed sha256 aggregate id, re-read durable authority instead of trusting the caller, commit under an event id copied rather than minted, answer from re-decoded bytes that still re-encode. Every production .ts here has a sibling .js bridge containing exactly `export * from "./<name>.ts";`.
planningNotes.risks:
1) `createDeadEndJournal` CRASHES ON A MALFORMED ENTRY rather than refusing — `clonePredicate` returns undefined for an unknown predicate kind and `canonicalSha256` throws on undefined. If the daemon's strict entry decode is missing or incomplete, the command dies with a TypeError and any test asserting only "did not succeed" stays green. Assert the REFUSAL code, and drill it by deleting the decoder.

2) `cloneEntry` SPREADS the caller's entry, so an extra key would survive into the journal AND into the digest. The exact-key entry decoder is the only thing preventing that; it is not defence in depth, it is the fence.

3) ADDING A WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY. `pnpm install` on this repo has known Windows hazards (a WSL-stamped node_modules kills Windows pnpm).
